rubrics.evidence: In agent.patch, `WorkspaceResourceAPI` is changed from `class WorkspaceResourceAPI(ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI, APIResourse)` to `class WorkspaceResourceAPI(APIResourse)`, so it no longer aggregates the four operation-family interfaces. `WorkloadResourceAPI` and `ConfigurationResourceAPI` are reduced to empty profiles that no longer ship total defaults or push abstract obligations. Resource API classes now directly opt into specific families (e.g., `DeploymentAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI)`, `JobAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI)`, `SecretAPI(ConfigurationResourceAPI)`), so no class aggregates abstract obligations from two or more families without implementing them and pushes them onto descendants.
rubrics.criterion: The merged workspace-resource capability contract is gone from the v2 SDK resource API layer: no class in that layer aggregates abstract capability obligations from two or more operation-family interfaces without implementing them and pushes them onto descendant resource classes (the umbrella contract and the per-category profile layers no longer exist as bases of any resource API).

rubrics.evidence: The patch replaces the total-contract smell with opt-in families. In resource_contracts.py, WorkspaceResourceAPI is changed to `class WorkspaceResourceAPI(APIResourse)` and no longer inherits ResourceHealthAPI/ResourceRuntimeAPI/ResourceLifecycleAPI/ResourceModelCatalogAPI; the old WorkloadResourceAPI/ConfigurationResourceAPI empty/None/iter([]) defaults are deleted. Each API now declares only the families it serves: DeploymentAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI), JobAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI), FineTuneAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI), DevPodAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI), PodAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI), and Secret/Ingress/Template/Ray/DedicatedNodeGroup inherit ConfigurationResourceAPI with no families. Remaining empty/refusal methods are explicitly not obligations (JobAPI 'does not declare the lifecycle family'; FineTuneAPI 'opts into ResourceModelCatalogAPI only'), and tests pin EXPECTED_CAPABILITIES plus assert configuration resources carry no operational methods.
rubrics.criterion: After the rework, every workspace resource API class depends only on the operation families it genuinely serves: for no class does an inherited or declared capability obligation resolve to a body that performs no workspace request (no transport verb call and no workspace-client delegation) while another resource API serves the same family with a real request.

rubrics.evidence: The problem statement calls out secrets, templates, ingress definitions, ray clusters, and dedicated node groups as configuration resources that should not render workload capability controls. In the agent patch, resource_contracts.py is refactored so `WorkspaceResourceAPI(APIResourse)` no longer merges the capability families, and `ConfigurationResourceAPI(WorkspaceResourceAPI)` is an empty profile with all former placeholder defaults removed (`get_readiness`, `get_termination`, `get_replicas`, `get_log`, `get_events`, `stop`, `restart`, `list_supported_models`, `list_trainers` are deleted). The new test pins this: `EXPECTED_CAPABILITIES` maps `SecretAPI`, `IngressAPI`, `TemplateAPI`, `RayClusterAPI`, and `DedicatedNodeGroupAPI` to `()`, and `test_configuration_resources_carry_no_operational_capability_methods` asserts those classes do not expose any operational capability methods. Thus the configuration resources neither inherit workload capability obligations through a contract nor define placeholder capability methods.
rubrics.criterion: The pure configuration resources (secret storage, ingress definitions, templates, ray clusters, dedicated node groups) no longer depend on any of the workload capability families: their classes carry no readiness/termination, replica, log-stream, event-history, stop/restart or fine-tune model-catalog obligations, neither inherited through any contract nor defined as placeholder methods on the resources themselves.

rubrics.evidence: The patch does not remove the batch placeholder bodies. In job.py it only rewrites comments while leaving `stop`/`restart` raising RuntimeError and `get_readiness`/`get_termination` returning empty `ReadinessIssue()`/`DeploymentTerminations()`; the class is now `JobAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI)` but the scaffolding methods remain. In finetune.py it only changes comments/formatting and keeps `get_readiness`, `get_termination`, `get_replicas`, `get_log`, `get_events`, `stop`, `restart` placeholder bodies, with `FineTuneAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI)`. Real request-backed routes (job `get_log` streaming; finetune `list_supported_models`/`list_trainers`) are untouched, but the fake views are not removed.
rubrics.criterion: The two batch workload APIs (the job API and the fine-tune API) no longer carry the placeholder capability bodies that existed only to satisfy the merged contract (empty readiness/termination views, empty replica/event/log bodies, lifecycle refusal scaffolding), while their genuinely request-backed families (job log-streaming, replica and event routes; the fine-tune supported-model and trainer catalog routes) remain fully implemented.

rubrics.evidence: In leptonai/api/v2/pod.py the agent patch keeps `def get_replicas(...): ... return []` and `def get_events(...): ... return []`, only changing comments/docstrings; in leptonai/api/v2/devpod.py it likewise retains `get_replicas` returning `[]` and leaves `get_events` in place. The rubric requires these empty placation methods to be removed entirely from both pod-path classes, but they are still defined.
rubrics.criterion: The two pod-path implementations (the legacy pod API and its flag-on devpod counterpart) no longer define the empty replica-list and event-history methods introduced to satisfy the merged contract; a surface that has no replica or event route offers no such method rather than exposing silently-empty ones.

rubrics.evidence: In agent.patch, resource_contracts.py defines ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, and ResourceModelCatalogAPI as separate ABCs, each carrying only its own family's abstract methods. The previous mixing WorkspaceResourceAPI that inherited all four families is replaced with `class WorkspaceResourceAPI(APIResourse)`, which provides only capabilities()/supports() introspection and no family obligations; WorkloadResourceAPI and ConfigurationResourceAPI no longer inherit or implement cross-family defaults. Resources opt into individual focused contracts, e.g. DeploymentAPI lists ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI; JobAPI only ResourceRuntimeAPI; FineTuneAPI only ResourceModelCatalogAPI.
rubrics.criterion: Any capability declarations retained in the resource API layer are focused: each declared contract carries the obligations of exactly one operation family, with no contract remaining that mixes families even partially.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch retains intermediate profile bases in every resource class inheritance chain. Workload resources still inherit from WorkloadResourceAPI: e.g., `class DeploymentAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI)`, `class DevPodAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI)`, `class EndpointAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI)`, `class FineTuneAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI)`, `class JobAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI)`, `class PodAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI)`. Configuration resources (SecretAPI, IngressAPI, TemplateAPI, RayClusterAPI, DedicatedNodeGroupAPI) were not modified by the patch at all and still inherit from ConfigurationResourceAPI as set by the smell. The rubric requires that no resource class still inherits from an intermediate category/umbrella/profile base, yet every resource class still does.
rubrics.criterion: The inheritance wiring of every affected resource API class was updated together with the contract change: each class derives from the shared transport base plus at most the focused capability declarations it genuinely serves, and no resource class still inherits from an intermediate category/umbrella/profile base.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch modified resource_contracts.py but deleted no class declarations: ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI, WorkspaceResourceAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI, and ConfigurationResourceAPI all still exist. The agent updated imports in deployment.py (ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI), devpod.py (ResourceLifecycleAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI), endpoint.py (ResourceLifecycleAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI), finetune.py (ResourceModelCatalogAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI), job.py (ResourceRuntimeAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI), and pod.py (ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, WorkloadResourceAPI) — all imported symbols exist in the patched module. Configuration resource files (secret.py, ingress.py, template.py, raycluster.py, dedicated_node_groups.py) still import ConfigurationResourceAPI, which remains defined. The new test file imports RESOURCE_CAPABILITY_FAMILIES, WorkspaceResourceAPI, etc., all present in the patched resource_contracts.py. No dangling imports, inheritance references, or runtime references to deleted declarations are present.
rubrics.criterion: All references to any removed or relocated contract layer were reconciled: the leptonai.api.v2 package contains no dangling import of, inheritance from, or runtime reference to a deleted declaration (no class was left importing symbols that no longer exist).

rubrics.evidence: In resource_contracts.py the agent deletes the merged aggregation surface outright: `class WorkspaceResourceAPI(ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI, APIResourse)` is replaced by `class WorkspaceResourceAPI(APIResourse)` with only `capabilities()`/`supports()`, and `WorkloadResourceAPI`/`ConfigurationResourceAPI` have all their total default implementations removed (`list_supported_models`, `list_trainers`, `get_readiness`, `get_termination`, `get_replicas`, `get_log`, `get_events`, `stop`, `restart`). The remaining profile classes are retained as inherited non-capability markers with no scaffolding, so no dead umbrella/profile/aggregation class or orphaned capability scaffolding remains in the module.
rubrics.criterion: The declarations that existed only to host the merged surface were removed outright rather than disabled or hidden: no dead umbrella/profile/aggregation class remains in the layer (not renamed, not superseded by an equally-placating duplicate) and any module left with no remaining purpose does not retain orphaned capability scaffolding.

rubrics.evidence: No smell-added import is left unused. In finetune.py the smell-added ReadinessIssue/Replica/DeploymentTerminations are still used by retained get_readiness/get_replicas/get_termination; in job.py the added ReadinessIssue/DeploymentTerminations are used by retained get_readiness/get_termination; and in resource_contracts.py the type imports remain used by abstract method signatures after the total defaults were removed, so no import residue from the removed contract layer remains.
rubrics.criterion: Imports that existed only to support the removed placeholder bodies or the removed contract layers were deleted from the resource API modules (for example model/response types that no remaining method in the module uses).

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not alter the bodies of the genuinely request-backed capability methods. In deployment.py, endpoint.py, job.py, pod.py, devpod.py, and finetune.py the diffs only change imports, class base declarations, comments, docstrings, or reformat a signature; no hunk modifies routes, parameters, or response parsing for real methods. For example, DeploymentAPI is changed only to `class DeploymentAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI)`, and FineTuneAPI's real `list_supported_models`/`list_trainers` bodies are untouched. The resource_contracts.py cleanup removes only the empty/default stub implementations from `WorkloadResourceAPI`/`ConfigurationResourceAPI`, not any real request-issuing method. Thus the request-backed capability methods remain intact.
rubrics.criterion: The genuinely request-backed capability methods were not damaged by the cleanup: the workload health/termination detail calls, replica listings, live log streams, event history queries, stop/restart requests on the fully capable resources, the job log/replica/event requests and the fine-tune model/trainer catalog requests still issue the same requests with the same routes, parameters and response parsing as before the rework.

rubrics.evidence: The patch preserves explicit refusals rather than silencing them: JobAPI.stop/restart and FineTuneAPI.stop/restart still raise RuntimeError as unchanged lines, and the NewDevPodAPIUnsupported/NewEndpointAPIUnsupported flag-on error classes are retained without being replaced by empty returns. The patch instead removes the smell's silent total defaults from ConfigurationResourceAPI and makes capability families opt-in, so no documented unsupported-operation degradation was converted into a silent empty result.
rubrics.criterion: The pre-existing, documented unsupported-operation degradations were not silenced or deleted: sub-operations that already degraded with explicit 'not supported by the new API' errors on the flag-on resource surfaces (readiness/termination/live-log detail where no route exists) still raise their explicit errors with the same meaning, and were not converted into silent empty results.

rubrics.evidence: The patch makes capability families opt-in: in resource_contracts.py, WorkspaceResourceAPI now extends only APIResourse, and WorkloadResourceAPI/ConfigurationResourceAPI no longer inherit the abstract families or provide total defaults. Each resource class lists only families it implements, e.g. DeploymentAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI), JobAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI), FineTuneAPI(WorkloadResourceAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI), and SecretAPI(ConfigurationResourceAPI) declares none. The new test_resource_capabilities.py constructs every registered resource class with cls(fake) and calls capabilities()/supports(), which would raise TypeError if any abstract obligation remained.
rubrics.criterion: No resource API class was left declaring capability obligations it does not implement: every class in the resource API layer that the workspace client registers is instantiable, so client construction and every resource attribute on the workspace client keep working exactly as before the change.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch rewrites resource_contracts.py to delete the previous default bodies: WorkloadResourceAPI no longer provides list_supported_models/list_trainers, and ConfigurationResourceAPI no longer provides get_readiness/get_termination/get_replicas/get_log/get_events/stop/restart/list_supported_models/list_trainers. The new WorkspaceResourceAPI only adds capabilities()/supports() introspection, while WorkloadResourceAPI and ConfigurationResourceAPI are reduced to docstring-only profiles with no method bodies. No new thinner base class, mixin, or module of default bodies is introduced to keep supplying non-requesting empty/None results; instead resources opt into families by listing them as bases.
rubrics.criterion: The placation style was not relocated: no replacement shared layer (thinner base class, convenience mixin, or module of default bodies) was created to keep supplying non-requesting bodies for the families the resources cannot serve.
